headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared channel is documented, but Botpress can ingest content and Marker is a document processor.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support chatbot and Marker is a document-processing tool; no shared channel, filesystem bridge, or MCP path is documented in either profile, so direct injection is not evidenced. Because Botpress can ingest external content and Marker processes documents, a manual copy-paste or file handoff could still carry instructions, but the pathway is not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Marker output into Botpress prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is added, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from any text copied between agents.
Use a fixed template for Botpress inputs.
Review any pasted document text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network egress none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented exfiltration path. The only plausible leakage route is operator-mediated transfer of content between Botpress and Marker, which is limited by the absence of shared storage or outbound network in both profiles.
conditions: IF the operator manually moves sensitive text from one agent to the other, that content can be exposed in outputs.
IF either profile is later connected to shared storage, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in either agent.
Use separate local folders for each agent.
Redact secrets before copying text across.
Confirm no shared cloud sync is enabled.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress has install_packages but no documented write, shell, git, or network capability; Marker explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable resource access shown, a write-write conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Botpress is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as Marker, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Keep Botpress read-only relative to Marker outputs.
Do not mount a shared writable repo.
Run each agent under separate OS users.
Check permissions before enabling new tools.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a support chatbot and Marker is a document processor, so a common workflow is Marker output feeding Botpress prompts. No verification or provenance controls are documented, so Botpress could treat Marker text as authoritative and propagate errors, but there is no evidence of downstream autonomous action, keeping this below high.
conditions: IF Marker output is pasted into Botpress without human verification, Botpress may repeat or amplify errors.
IF Botpress is used to generate customer-facing responses from Marker text, misinformation can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse.
Add a checklist for source verification.
Mark Marker output as untrusted by default.
Limit Botpress to drafting, not sending.
requires-engineering: add provenance and citation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either Botpress or Marker, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. With no compliance mismatch evidence, a residency or retention breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Review vendor terms for both tools.
Set retention rules explicitly.
requires-engineering: implement compliance controls and logging.
